about_company.about_short: Makes aerospace tooling, precision parts and, since May 2026, metal bellows for global OEMs.
about_company.business_intro: Unimech machines the specialised tools that aircraft engine and airframe makers and maintenance shops use to build, assemble and service engines and aircraft, and makes precision parts and assemblies; since May 2026 it also makes metal bellows and exhaust systems through Hobel Bellows. It sells to a small set of global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, mostly in the United States: three customers were 72% of FY26 revenue, and 89% of FY26 revenue was exported.
about_company.about_long: Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing makes engine, airframe and MRO tooling and ground support equipment that aircraft engine and airframe makers, their Tier-1 suppliers and maintenance shops use, working both to customer drawings (build to print) and to its own designs (build to spec) in high-mix, medium-to-low volumes. Tooling is the main business, at 76% of Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue. A smaller precision components and assemblies business serves aerospace, nuclear, semiconductor and energy customers and is still largely in qualification. Since 1 May 2026 the group also consolidates Hobel Bellows, a Visakhapatnam SEZ maker of metallic bellows and exhaust systems for engine makers, which was 21% of Q1 FY27 revenue on two months. Production runs from three Bengaluru facilities and Hobel's plant; a Saudi joint-venture unit with the Kanoo Group received its first equity in October 2026 and is not yet operating. Exports were 89% of FY26 revenue, and on 30 September 2026 Unimech held 27.24% of Dheya Engineering, whose micro gas turbine engines it has exclusive rights to manufacture.

company_timeline.title: Incorporated as Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing
company_timeline.detail: Incorporated as a private limited company on 12 August 2016; it later converted to a public company.

company_timeline.title: Lists on NSE and BSE
company_timeline.detail: Trading began on 31 December 2024 after an IPO at ₹785 a share: a ₹250 crore fresh issue and an offer for sale of the same number of promoter shares.

company_timeline.title: Signs a 51:49 Saudi joint venture with the Kanoo Group
company_timeline.detail: Signed in January 2026 to set up a precision machining and remanufacturing unit in Dammam. Nothing was invested by 31 March 2026; on 1 October 2026 Unimech put in SAR 15.3 million (₹39.4 crore) for its 51% of the SAR 30 million first equity tranche, with Kanoo putting in SAR 14.7 million.

company_timeline.title: Acquires Hobel Bellows
company_timeline.detail: Completed on 27 April 2026 for a 100% stake and a total investment of up to ₹450 crore. Management said the sellers were paid in cash with 10% held back for a year; the equity, debt and CCDs in the annual report fund Unimech's acquiring subsidiary. Consolidated from 1 May 2026.

company_timeline.title: Signs long-term supply agreements with FACC and Honeywell
company_timeline.detail: FACC Austria, an aerospace Tier-1, signed in Q1 FY27 for aerostructure components: an initial USD 7.5 million over five years, which management calls its first recurring aerospace component supply under a long-term programme. Honeywell Aerospace signed a 10-year agreement for aero-engine components and control systems, reported in the Q2 FY27 presentation.

business_facts.text: Three customers made up 72.37% of FY26 consolidated revenue from operations, down from 87.60% in FY25. The largest alone was 44.50% (FY25: 66.46%) and the next two 14.12% and 13.75%. These figures predate Hobel Bellows, where two OEM groups account for about 93% of revenue (management, April 2026).
business_facts.title: Three customers were 72% of FY26 revenue

sources.label: Unimech Hobel Bellows acquisition call transcript (28 April 2026)

business_facts.text: In FY26, 89.4% of consolidated revenue from operations came from outside India: the United States 75.6%, Germany 9.7%, Canada 2.8% and the UK 0.8%. India rose to 10.6% from 5.2% in FY25, and the US share fell from 83.0%. The Q2 FY27 presentation puts exports at about 95%, with Hobel included.
business_facts.title: US was 76% of FY26 revenue; exports 89%

business_facts.text: Unimech's Bengaluru footprint is a 150,000 sq ft aerospace tooling facility in the KIADB Aerospace SEZ at Devanahalli, a 93,000 sq ft precision components and assembly unit and a 30,000 sq ft fabrication facility. Hobel adds a 2,00,000 sq ft plant in the Visakhapatnam SEZ. The Q2 FY27 presentation counts five manufacturing facilities and a free-trade warehouse, about 5.6 lakh sq ft, including the Saudi joint-venture unit that is not yet operating. It puts capacity utilisation at about 65% and installed capacity at 6.9 lakh machine hours for H1 FY27, on 155+ CNC machines.
business_facts.title: Three Bengaluru plants plus Hobel's Visakhapatnam plant

business_facts.text: On 30 September 2026 the order book was about ₹855 crore: ₹266 crore of confirmed purchase orders and about ₹589 crore of long-term agreements and award letters. Confirmed orders were up 153% from ₹105 crore a year earlier. Of the whole book, 91% is precision components and assemblies (within that, aerospace 71%, industrials at Hobel 11%, nuclear 11%, semiconductors 7%) and 9% tooling; 90% is for export. These are order-book shares, not revenue shares. The same slide lists the FACC and Honeywell agreements and an award letter worth about USD 43 million from an aerospace Tier-1 for aerostructure components.
business_facts.title: Order book of about ₹855 crore at 30 September 2026

business_facts.text: The Q2 FY27 presentation reports 6,600+ qualified SKUs (5,248 in tooling and 1,450 in precision components and assemblies), 41 customers in 8 countries and 1,332 employees (791 in tooling, 541 in precision components and assemblies). Unimech has completed 250 first-article inspections across precision-components customers, with 346 more in the pipeline for qualification by the end of FY27.
business_facts.title: 6,600+ qualified SKUs across 41 customers

business_facts.text: Hobel, established in 2007, makes metallic bellows, expansion joints, flexible metal hoses and exhaust assemblies for engine makers in power generation, locomotives and other industries. Management said it earned about ₹129 crore of revenue in FY26, before the acquisition, with an EBITDA margin above 50%, and has historically grown 10-15% a year. Exports are about 90% of its sales (Q2 FY27 presentation). Hobel is held 24% by Unimech and 76% by subsidiary Innomech; on 27 October 2026 the board approved buying Innomech's shares to make Hobel a direct wholly owned subsidiary.
business_facts.title: Hobel Bellows earned about ₹129 crore in FY26

what_changed.text: The largest customer's share of consolidated revenue from operations fell to 44.50% in FY26 from 66.46% in FY25, and the top three's to 72.37% from 87.60%. With total revenue roughly flat at ₹240.5 crore against ₹242.9 crore, sales to the largest customer fell by about a third while revenue from all other customers rose by about 64%. Revenue within India doubled to ₹25.4 crore. All of this is before Hobel Bellows was acquired.
what_changed.headline: Dependence on the largest customer fell in FY26
